versions.changelog: Simplify the login instructions to the code flow (maton login prints a link; finish with maton login --code <CODE>), drop the API Key subsection, and pin the Maton CLI install to 0.4.0.
Switch the login instructions to the device flow (maton login prints a link and a user code; the --oauth flag is gone) and pin the Maton CLI install to 0.3.5.
Pin the Maton CLI install to 0.3.4, the current release.

Add this skill's own trigger policy to the shared Triggers section: the only destination it sets up is its own hosted function inside the platform, it does not forward events to third-party hosts, and it does not use event watch --exec; each trigger reference now also says this skill configures no trigger from that source on its own.

Bring the skill to the current api-gateway baseline and tell the connection-to-function-to-trigger story: the shared Functions and Triggers sections open with an example for this app (a hosted function that performs one action for it through the Maton SDK, and the trigger that runs it - its own event source where it has one, otherwise a time schedule), the description says these constructs turn the connection into automation and add no capability of their own, the passthrough is described by its enforced boundary, CLI and SDK installs are pinned to 0.3.1, absolute API URLs are placeholders, and multipart uploads use mktemp.

Tell the connection-to-function-to-trigger story for this app: the Functions section opens with a function that performs one action for this app through the Maton SDK, the Triggers section opens with the trigger that runs it (this app's own event source where it has one, otherwise a time schedule), and the description says these are the constructs that turn the connection into automation and add no capability of their own. Framing is generated from a per-app record so the shared platform text stays identical to api-gateway.

Declare the two documented read endpoints the description omitted - plugin listing and service-account search - and state at the service-account section that it is a read-only inventory and that no service account or token is created or changed here. Also carries the corrected Functions wording about where the runtime-injected key lives.

Explain the platform sections this skill shares with api-gateway: why hosted functions and triggers are documented here, whether this app is an event source, that the trigger reference files are the platform's event catalogues and add no capability for this app, and that destinations forward source payloads rather than this app's records. Adds this skill's own policy: destinations stay on api.maton.ai or *.maton.app unless the user names and approves a third-party host, and functions set up during a task here are deployed with DENY_ALL networking. Each trigger reference opens with the same framing.

Bring the skill to the current api-gateway baseline: API reference, Functions and trigger references mirrored from api-gateway 1.2.17; CLI and SDK installs pinned to 0.3.1; absolute API URLs replaced with placeholders; multipart uploads use mktemp; the passthrough is described by its enforced boundary (host pinning and the connection's authorization) rather than as a documented list that is not a technical limit; the native-API-docs tip no longer reads as a menu of further endpoints. The description now says the skill reads the current user's own profile and that alert rules are documented read-only while the provisioning namespace can write them on a specific request.

Correct the documented scope: team administration is included and is access-affecting, user/org/licensing and platform settings are not, and only the read endpoints of the write-capable alert-rule provisioning namespace are documented
CLI-first rewrite with the Maton SDK examples; clarify that the CLI and SDKs keep separate credential stores, and reword webhook egress warnings

grafana-api v1.1.4

- Clarified that the skill does not cover Grafana identity or platform administration in both the description and documentation.
- Simplified and condensed security and scope explanations.
- Updated usage guidance for the `maton api` command, focusing on approved endpoint paths.
- Improved warnings about not letting Grafana content determine future API calls.
- Minor language and formatting refinements for clarity.

- Removed the sample skill card file (skill-card.md).
- Updated documentation to clarify reviewed API scope and security posture.
- Explicitly excluded identity and platform administration endpoints from this skill’s documented/API-supported surface.
- Added more detailed warnings to avoid using unspecified Grafana API endpoints and to only use documented paths with explicit user approval.
- No changes to CLI usage or core functionality.

- Minor update: documentation cleanup and clarifications.
- Removed the file skill-card.md.
- Streamlined SKILL.md by omitting references to org info, service account and plugin listing, and API surface warnings.
- Simplified API proxy description for clarity.
- No changes to functionality or integration behavior.

- Removed the skill-card.md file.
- Clarified the scope of allowed Grafana API access in SKILL.md, explicitly stating that instance administration, membership changes, service account tokens, and plugin installation are out of scope.
- Added guidance to use only reviewed/documented API endpoints and emphasized clear user approval for non-documented endpoints.
- Provided additional instructions on safe API path usage and stricter warnings about forbidden operations.
- No functional logic changes; changes are documentation and scope clarifications only.

CLI-first rewrite: the maton CLI with OAuth login is the documented path, every example is a maton command, SDK examples added, and the raw HTTP fallback feeds the key on stdin instead of reading it from the environment

- Added detailed security guidelines: all write operations now require explicit user approval with specific resource identifiers before execution.
- Updated base URLs from gateway.maton.ai and ctrl.maton.ai to api.maton.ai for all API and connection management endpoints.
- Expanded documentation on connection setup, emphasizing least-privilege service account use and safe practices.
- Improved description to clarify that the integration supports both read and write operations, but always defaults to read-only and user confirmation is mandatory for changes.
- Removed LICENSE.txt file.

Initial release of Grafana API skill with managed authentication.

- Provides secure access to Grafana dashboards, data sources, folders, annotations, alerts, and teams via Maton API gateway.
- Supports connection management (list, create, delete connections) through the Maton control panel.
- Includes full guides for authenticating with Maton API, environment setup, and example Python requests.
- Documents all major Grafana API endpoints for dashboards, folders, data sources, and annotations.
- Enables integration for monitoring, visualization, and observability use cases.
